s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of focal upper limb weakness
salient_findings: Sudden weakness of the left upper limb
Weakness of the distal phalanx of the thumb and middle phalanx of the index finger
Decreased grip strength on the left
key_facts: Episodes of isolated, sudden weakness of the left upper limb
No muscular wasting, pathological reflexes, or focal neurological signs
Electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve
MRI of the left upper extremity showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Anterior Interosseous Nerve Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve

shortlist.label: Neuralgic Amyotrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of focal upper limb weakness and electromyographic findings

shortlist.label: Parsonage-Turner Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of weakness and electromyographic evidence of neurogenic atrophy

shortlist.label: Hirayama Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Focal upper limb weakness and absence of sensory deficits

shortlist.label: Mononeuritis Multiplex
shortlist.why_kept: Electromyographic evidence of neurogenic atrophy in multiple nerve distributions

raw.rationale: The electromyographic evaluation showed neurogenic atrophy of muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve, which directly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neuralgic Amyotrophy
rejected.why: While it involves nerve damage, it typically presents with more widespread shoulder and arm pain and weakness, not isolated to the anterior interosseous nerve distribution.

rejected.label: Parsonage-Turner Syndrome
rejected.why: Similar to Neuralgic Amyotrophy, it involves more widespread brachial plexus inflammation and does not specifically target the anterior interosseous nerve.

rejected.label: Hirayama Disease
rejected.why: Characterized by progressive muscular atrophy of the distal upper limb, often with cold paresis, which does not match the sudden, isolated episodes described.

rejected.label: Mononeuritis Multiplex
rejected.why: Involves damage to at least two separate peripheral nerves, which does not align with the specific involvement of the anterior interosseous nerve in this case.
